items.elements: Very low song (about 0.5 kHz with stacked harmonics up to 2 kHz): a faint short lead-in near 0.3 s, then six arched, hooting notes of about equal length (about 0.8 to 3.1 s), with the last one sliding down into a falling tail around 3.3 to 3.6 s.
items.phrase: so, who knew you'd move through to-o-o
items.grounds: One short soft syllable for the faint lead-in, then six low, round 'oo' words of even length for the arched hoots, with the last one stretched to follow the falling tail; the 'oo' vowel sound came from how low and hollow the harmonic arches look, not from any bird I know.

items.elements: A two-part unit repeated eight times, getting louder and higher: a sharp high downslur (about 7 down to 4.5 kHz) followed by a lower V-shaped downsweep (about 4 down to 2.5 kHz). There is one lone low note at the start and a buzzy lower note at the end (about 2.9 s).
items.phrase: a PICK-up PICK-up PICK-up PICK-up PICK-up PICK-up PICK-up PICK-up, then
items.grounds: The picture shows eight strong-weak pairs, the first part high and sharp and the second lower, growing louder, with one pickup note and one closing note, so I wrote a two-syllable word stressed on the first syllable, eight times; to be honest, I recognised the pattern as the known 'teacher-teacher' mnemonic and deliberately avoided that word, but that knowledge probably shaped my choice of a stress-first two-beat word.

items.elements: An opening falling note, then two identical three-part figures (a rising slur from about 2.6 to 4.3 kHz, a short high tick near 6.3 kHz, a long descent from 5.5 to 2.8 kHz). After a gap comes a louder, harsher ending (1.3 to 1.85 s): a buzz near 3.5 kHz, a very steep upsweep to about 10 kHz, a rising slur, and a sharp drop.
items.phrase: so, here we go, here we go, buzz zip zing zap
items.grounds: 'so' is the first falling note; each 'here we go' follows one rise-tick-fall figure, with 'go' drawn out for the long descent; the four harsh one-syllable words match the dark, buzzy, steeply swept ending, and all of it came from the picture, not from any knowledge of a species.

items.elements: Two long, slow rising slurs (about 1.8 up to 3.2 kHz; the second is longer, about 0.5 s), followed by five short, evenly spaced, loud downslurs (about 3.5 down to 1.7 kHz), each with a faint harmonic above.
items.phrase: Why? Whyyy? Down, down, down, down, down.
items.grounds: The two long rising slurs look like a voice rising on a question, with the second one stretched longer, and the five quick sharp downstrokes look like a word stressed hard at the start that drops, so the words follow the shapes directly; none came from knowledge of a bird.

items.elements: A busy, irregular song: a broadband click (about 0.27 s), a long rising slur (1.7 to 3.2 kHz) that ends in a sharp peak-and-drop, two broadband ticks (about 0.9 to 1.0 s), a falling note near 2.8 kHz, a low dip, a quick rise-and-fall hook near 4 kHz, a short low note, a very high upsweep (about 1.5 s), and a final sharp downstroke. Background noise is heavy.
items.phrase: Tick. Sli-i-ide up SNAP! chk chk, sigh, dip, flip, bump, ZIP, drop.
items.grounds: Each word stands for one mark in the order they come: a long stretched 'slide up' for the long rising slur, 'snap' for its sharp peak, clicky words for the broadband ticks, a falling 'sigh', and a stressed 'ZIP' for the tall high upsweep; it all came from the picture, though the count is uncertain because the cut is noisy.
